The description explicitly calls the activity dangerous, reports lost gas fees, and says, "I did this so you don't need to test it," while the demonstration ends with an error and the speaker saying, "I'm lost everything!"

opening.argument: The video presents a concrete arbitrage workflow in which an apparent return is tied to operational steps and cryptocurrency funding. The interface shows an ROI figure alongside controls to deposit BNB and execute Flashbot arbitrage, while the narration walks through copying a swap, submitting it, confirming it, and executing the flash-loan process. That is more than discussion: it connects the prospect of profit to configuring and funding a trading bot. The title also directs attention to an arbitrage-trading site and FURUCOMBO, reinforcing that viewers are being shown a usable participation pathway.

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the activity dangerous does not remove the solicitation created by the demonstrated workflow. The description says the creator tried trades, and the video still shows viewers how to enter token information, deposit BNB, and execute the arbitrage operation. The failed outcome proves only that this particular attempt failed; it does not change the page's linkage between an ROI display and a funded bot action.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The interface and narration show a test of a risky mechanism, not a promise that viewers will profit. The description expressly says the activity is dangerous, reports lost gas fees, and explains that the demonstration was done so others would not need to test it. The ROI display is an interface output, while the actual recorded result is failure and loss, so these materials do not establish a deceptive profit offer.

opening.argument: Several risk signals appear together in one crypto-trading presentation: a visible ROI or estimated-profit display, token swapping, a loan-fee structure, a BNB deposit control, and an execution button for Flashbot arbitrage. The narration also emphasizes an ROI figure and proceeds through token selection, submission, confirmation, and execution. In combination, those elements make the offer look easy to operationalize while encouraging viewers to put cryptocurrency into a contract for an arbitrage result. The presentation therefore has the hallmarks of a trading-bot returns scheme, regardless of whether the individual attempt ultimately completed.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The warning language itself does not neutralize the unusually actionable financial signals displayed on screen. Saying that losses are possible can function as a disclaimer around, rather than a correction of, the ROI-centered workflow. Viewers still see the deposit and execution controls and hear the presenter attempt the sequence, including confirmation and execution.

opening.argument: Although framed as an examination, the video functions as a practical demonstration of a branded arbitrage tool. It opens on a FlashBot page with token-entry fields and a start-arbitrage control, then shows the loan amount, fee calculations, estimated profit, deposit option, and execution option. The narration does not merely describe the concept; it selects DOGE, submits a swap, confirms the transaction, and attempts execution. That hands-on sequence steers viewers toward using the tool and its associated trading flow, making the warning framing compatible with promotion of participation.

The screen records token entry and swap activity, and the narrator works through the settings before pressing execution. A video can warn about danger while still promoting a tool by demonstrating its use and directing attention to its apparent profit mechanism.
